intro: Don't aim for perfect prompts today. Once workflows run for real, prompts will change in ways we can't predict from the desk. Today's job is knowing where the good material lives so we can assemble per-problem in minutes.

headline.richest_source: AWB Gen 3 — 31 production .hbs prompts with paired .json schemas
headline.second_richest: Baku FliLaunch — 12 analysis + 4 packaging prompts in one TS file
headline.unique_ip: Baku FliLaunch p06 audience classification — only prompt that decides badge-vs-title placement of identity terms

prompts.name: FliLaunch v2 — 12-prompt analysis bank
prompts.description: p01 core idea, p02 key value, p03 hook angles, p04 audience hints, p05 identity keywords, p06 audience classification, p07 emotional tone, p08 topic keywords, p09 takeaways, p10 questions, p11 unique angle, p12 related signals. Has placeholders + JSON shapes + focal_note + known_audiences footer.

prompts.name: B-YouTube-Launch-Optimizer — 12 default analysis prompts
prompts.description: Predecessor of Baku FliLaunch. Worth comparing for prompts the new set dropped — Memorable Quotes, Visual Themes, Controversial Claims, CTA opportunities.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — 11 content-analysis Handlebars prompts
prompts.description: analyze-audience-insights, analyze-catchy-phrases, analyze-cta-phrases, analyze-emotional-triggers, analyze-key-takeaways, analyze-keywords, analyze-main-topic, analyze-overall-tone, analyze-questions-posed, analyze-search-terms, analyze-statistics, analyze-usp. Each .hbs paired with .json schema. Most polished analysis set.

prompts.name: ALS-Workflows phase2 procedure (12-dim grid)
prompts.description: Procedure doc not extractable templates. Differs from Baku — has p10 = Call to Action (instead of Questions), p12 = Engagement Hooks (instead of Related signals).

prompts.name: FliLaunch v2 — generating-hooks delamain agent
prompts.description: Generates 10–20 hook angles spanning 7 hook types (x_vs_y, only_one_worked, i_tried_x, problem_solution, contrarian_take, capability_demo, qualifying_question). Ranks top-4, marks AI #1 pick. Effectively a meta-hook prompt.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — analyze-catchy-phrases
prompts.description: Pulls quotable hook-able phrases from transcript.

prompts.name: ALS-workflows phase2 — p03 hook angles
prompts.description: Declares hook angles as gating output; 5 distinct framings.

prompts.name: FliLaunch — TITLES_PER_HOOK_PROMPT
prompts.description: Generates N titles anchored to a specific hook angle, with audience placement rules and existing-title de-duplication. Strongest title prompt — ties hooks → titles directly.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — generate-title.hbs
prompts.description: Three Emotions Framework (Curiosity / Desire / Fear), character-limit guidance, power words table, anti-clickbait rules.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — select-title-shortlist.hbs
prompts.description: Interactive curation prompt — present, ask clarifying questions, then shortlist (NOT auto-select).

prompts.name: B-YouTube-Launch-Optimizer — titles_generate / titles_refine
prompts.description: 15-title generation with style mix; refine variant takes 'direction' feedback.

prompts.name: ALS-Workflows phase3-titles procedure
prompts.description: 5 variants per hook (problem-led, outcome-led, numeric, curiosity-gap, audience-named).

prompts.name: FliLaunch — THUMBNAIL_CONCEPTS_PER_HOOK_PROMPT
prompts.description: 2 concepts per hook, prose visual direction + 2 text overlay options + secondary-audience badge suggestion.

prompts.name: B-YouTube-Launch-Optimizer — thumbnails_generate
prompts.description: 6 unique concepts. CONCEPT/DESCRIPTION/VISUAL BRIEF format suitable for downstream image gen.

prompts.name: ALS-Workflows phase4-thumbnails procedure
prompts.description: Concept structure: Title/Hook/Text/Visual concept/Design style/Mood per hook.

prompts.name: AppyDave-thumbnail skill — concept generation (brand baked in)
prompts.description: AppyDave-brand specific. Typography-first concepts, 5 composition patterns, ghost watermark, hook text composed at gen time.

prompts.name: FliThumb — design-conversation system prompt
prompts.description: Closest thing to an explicit thumbnail-text prompt — but it's conversational, not a one-shot generator. Defines the model: primary text (overlay) vs subliminal text (embedded in scene). Framework you want; prompt itself needs reshaping for batch generation.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — generate-thumbnail-text.hbs
prompts.description: This IS the missing thumbnail-text prompt. Different framing from FliThumb (no primary/subliminal split — just punchy overlay text). Part 1 / Part 2 / Part 3 segments tied to title ideas (table format).

prompts.name: FliLaunch — DESCRIPTION_PROMPT
prompts.description: 2-3 sentence synopsis + 10–15 SEO keyword tags, hook-aligned.

prompts.name: B-YouTube-Launch-Optimizer — description_narrative
prompts.description: Engaging SEO-optimised description from analysis output.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — yt-write-description.hbs
prompts.description: Pure assembly prompt — full YouTube formatting rules baked in (*bold*, headings, auto-links). Best for final stage.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — yt-simple-description.hbs
prompts.description: Lighter-weight description variant.

prompts.name: ALS-Workflows phase6-describe procedure
prompts.description: 8-slot composition structure (Synopsis, Chapters, CTA primary, Affiliate, Related, CTA fold, Social, Legal). Procedure not a prompt, but defines the slot model.

prompts.name: FliLaunch — CHAPTERS_PROMPT
prompts.description: Generates 'M:SS title' markers, anchored to SRT if provided, else inferred at 150 wpm.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — identify-chapters.hbs
prompts.description: Extracts chapter-worthy boundaries from transcript.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — refine-chapters.hbs
prompts.description: Refines chapter titles for clarity / engagement.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — create-chapters.hbs
prompts.description: Semantic-search match of chapter hints to edited SRT timestamps. Handles raw vs edited transcript mismatch. Best chapter-timestamping prompt in the ecosystem.

prompts.name: B-YouTube-Launch-Optimizer — chapters_generate / chapters_refine / chapter_editor_refine
prompts.description: Three chapter-related variants in the predecessor optimizer.

prompts.name: FliLaunch v2 — generating-chapters agent
prompts.description: SRT-first extraction with fallback estimation, segment-name dedup, ≤100 char rule.

prompts.name: FliLaunch — p06_audience_classification (unique IP)
prompts.description: Classify each known audience term as primary/secondary/hidden + placement (title/badge/none). Not present elsewhere in the ecosystem. Drives the badge-vs-title decision.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — analyze-audience-insights.hbs
prompts.description: Extract audience signals from transcript.

prompts.name: FliLaunch — p05_identity_keywords
prompts.description: Extracts tribal/identity terms (BMAD, vibe coding, etc.).

prompts.name: FliLaunch — DESCRIPTION_PROMPT keyword_tags portion
prompts.description: 10–15 SEO tags, search-intent only (NOT identity signals). Embedded in description prompt; consider extracting standalone.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — analyze-keywords.hbs / analyze-search-terms.hbs
prompts.description: Separate keyword and search-intent extraction.

prompts.name: SYSTEM_PROMPT_ANALYST + SYSTEM_PROMPT_PACKAGER
prompts.description: Dual-role system prompts for analysis vs packaging stages.

prompts.name: FliThumb design partner system prompt
prompts.description: JSON-output design conversation contract.

prompts.name: B-YouTube-Launch-Optimizer per-stage system prompts
prompts.description: System text embedded in each stage_prompt entry.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — create-tweet.hbs / create-linkedin-post.hbs / add-to-video-list.hbs
prompts.description: Social cross-post and related-video registration.

prompts.name: FliLaunch — p12_related_signals
prompts.description: Prior/follow-up/companion topic detection.

prompts.name: AWB Gen 3 — video-preparation prompts
prompts.description: abridge.hbs, abridge-qa.hbs, configure.hbs, summarize-video.hbs. New territory not in FliLaunch — abridging long transcripts before main pipeline.

sources.name: AWB Gen 3
sources.character_description: AWB Gen 3 is your most polished prompt set — 31 production Handlebars (.hbs) files paired with .json output schemas, organised into six sub-folders covering content-analysis, chapter-processing, title-thumbnail, youtube-metadata, social-media, and video-preparation. Every prompt is template-driven and structured-output ready, with rules baked into the prompt body itself (formatting, character limits, anti-clickbait constraints). It's the closest thing in the ecosystem to a production-ready prompt library — the strongest default starting point for any new workflow.
strengths: Most polished + most prompts — covers 10 of 12 categories
Each prompt has paired JSON schema for structured output
Best chapter-timestamping prompt (create-chapters.hbs) and best description assembler (yt-write-description.hbs)
weaknesses: No audience-classification prompt (no badge-vs-title placement logic)
Heavier templates — more cognitive load to assemble than Baku one-liners

sources.name: Baku FliLaunch
sources.character_description: Baku FliLaunch is the densest single-file prompt source — 12 analysis prompts plus 4 packaging prompts (titles, thumbnails, description, chapters) all living in one TypeScript file with placeholders, JSON shapes, focal_note, and a known_audiences footer. It owns the unique IP of the ecosystem: p06 audience classification — the only prompt that decides whether an identity term goes in the title, on a badge, or stays hidden. Per-hook fan-out is built in: TITLES_PER_HOOK and THUMBNAIL_CONCEPTS_PER_HOOK both anchor outputs to a chosen hook angle.
strengths: Only home of audience classification (p06) — unique IP
Hook-anchored title and thumbnail prompts — built for fan-out
Compact + readable — easy to lift into a new workflow
weaknesses: TypeScript-embedded — needs lifting out for non-TS consumers
Keyword-tags are entangled with the description prompt (no standalone)

sources.name: Baku YT-Optimizer
sources.character_description: Baku YT-Optimizer is the predecessor of Baku FliLaunch — 12 default analysis prompts plus per-stage prompt definitions for titles, thumbnails, description, and chapters. Worth keeping around as a comparison artifact: it carries prompts the newer FliLaunch dropped, including Memorable Quotes, Visual Themes, Controversial Claims, and CTA opportunities. If a workflow ever needs one of those dropped dimensions, this is where it still lives.
strengths: Carries dropped prompts (quotes, visual themes, controversies, CTA ops)
Chapter-editor refine variant exists here only
weaknesses: Older — superseded for everything FliLaunch covers

sources.name: FliLaunch v2 Agents
sources.character_description: FliLaunch v2 agent files live under the .als/modules/fli-launch/v2/delamains/launch/agents/ tree as procedural agent contracts (markdown, not extractable templates). Two stand out: generating-hooks (10–20 hooks across 7 hook types with ranked top-4 and AI #1 pick) and generating-chapters (SRT-first extraction with fallback estimation). These read more like instruction docs than prompts, but the hook-generation logic is the canonical hook source for the ecosystem.
strengths: Canonical hook generator — 7 hook types, ranked top-4, AI pick marked
Robust chapter agent with SRT-first + fallback strategy
weaknesses: Procedural markdown — not lift-and-shift prompt templates
Narrow coverage — only hooks and chapters

sources.name: FliThumb
sources.character_description: FliThumb owns the thumbnail design conversation — its system prompt defines the conceptual model that nothing else in the ecosystem articulates: primary text (overlay) vs subliminal text (embedded in scene), and four contrast modes (Explain/Intrigue, Abstract/Concrete, Calm/Dramatic, Parallel). The framework is the value, not the prompt itself — the prompt is conversational and would need reshaping for batch one-shot generation.
strengths: Defines the four contrast modes — nothing else does
weaknesses: Conversational, not one-shot — needs reshaping for batch
No prompt picks the right contrast mode for a given title × hook

sources.name: AppyDave Thumbnail Skill
sources.character_description: The AppyDave Thumbnail Claude Code skill carries the brand-baked variant of thumbnail concept generation — typography-first concepts, 5 composition patterns, ghost watermark rules, and hook text composed at gen time. It's tightly bound to the AppyDave brand, so reuse outside that brand requires un-baking the brand assumptions. Best treated as a finished operator tool rather than a prompt to assemble from.
strengths: Brand-baked — works out of the box for AppyDave thumbnails
Composition patterns + ghost watermark rules already encoded
weaknesses: Brand-coupled — not portable to non-AppyDave workflows

gaps.name: Standalone primary-vs-subliminal thumbnail-text prompt
gaps.description: FliThumb framework exists (primary overlay vs subliminal embedded) but only inside an interactive system prompt. No one-shot version: given title + contrast mode + secondary audiences, output 3 primary + 3 subliminal text candidates.

gaps.name: Cross-video triage / health-check prompt
gaps.description: Nothing in the ecosystem. The 'is this video missing X' pattern doesn't exist as a cross-video prompt. The whole TRIAGE workflow column has no prompt corpus to draw from.

gaps.name: Contrast-mode selector
gaps.description: FliThumb defines 4 contrast modes (explain_intrigue, abstract_concrete, calm_dramatic, parallel) but no prompt picks the right mode for a given title × hook. Currently manual.

gaps.name: Related-video ranker
gaps.description: Every prompt mentions related videos; none rank/pick from a candidate list.

gaps.name: North Star / channel-strategy injection
gaps.description: Explicitly v2+ in spec; no prompt yet.
